# OpenPencil

Own the task end to end. For routine Board creation, this file is the complete operating contract.
Do not read a reference, CLI help, repository source, or browser state before the first build unless
the task is refinement, diagnosis, product code, or a real command reports a missing detail.
When exact target IDs and a frozen creation scenario are supplied, finish any mandatory memory lookup
in the same first read, then write the plan and build. Do not search memory, source, schemas, or
examples again before or after an authoritative result.

## Routine prompt to Board

Choose the least capable medium that preserves behavior:

| User need                                           | Build route                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Plain note or caption                               | `native_text`              |
| Titled idea, summary, decision, brief, or checklist | `native_card`              |
| One self-contained static process or topology       | Mermaid `native_diagram`   |
| Several editable artifacts with meaningful edges    | `board build --plan-file`  |
| Trusted interaction or persistent state             | TSX `code_object`          |
| Meaningful relationship between independent objects | Optional `connect_objects` |

Never use Mermaid or a Code Object merely for visual novelty. A specialist may advise taste or a
recipe, but is optional; OpenPencil alone resolves target and mutation authority.

Choose Mermaid only when one diagram artifact preserves the request. For independent cards, captions,
mixed native objects, or meaningful relationships, use one `board build --plan-file` composition.
For shell-sensitive source, write a temporary JSON plan with `apply_patch`; never use a heredoc.

For one headless `native_card`, budget rendered height before the first call: at the default 320-unit
width keep the body around 550 characters or less. For more copy, use width 480–640 and compress the
body instead of discovering the 720-unit ceiling through refusal. The 1,200-character schema maximum
does not guarantee narrow wrapped text will fit. Preserve facts with short labels and compact lines.

When exact Board IDs are supplied, use the bundled CLI directly—never browser authoring or a shell
wrapper around the CLI:

```sh
/Users/omar/.codex/skills/openpencil/scripts/openpencil-cli.sh board build --fresh-context \
  --runtime-instance-id RUNTIME --workspace-id WORKSPACE --document-id DOCUMENT \
  --content-document-id CONTENT --page-id PAGE --request-id STABLE_ID \
  --intent 'Short user intent' --recipe 'RECIPE_JSON' --json
```
The bundled launcher defaults Board builds to the compact release envelope; it keeps authority,
proof, timing, and the deterministic final. Set `OPENPENCIL_OUTPUT=json` only for diagnosis.
Placement is explicit:

- No requested location: for a single recipe add `--auto-place` and omit `recipe.placement`; for `--plan-file`, the compiled plan owns placement (`--auto-place` is accepted but redundant).
- Beside an exact ID, use a relative target; beside a unique top-level name, use
  `--relative-to-name 'Exact name'` and let the CLI fail on missing/duplicate/truncated evidence.
- Exact Trace point or bounded area: use point or region placement. A point is one exact center and
  never auto-shifts when blocked; in plans, prefer one placed first artifact and alias-relative rest.
- Keep `preferred_directions` and `clearance` beside `target` inside `placement`, never inside target.

For a named relationship, use `board connect --fresh-context --source-name 'Source' --target-name
'Target' --kind visual --label 'explains'`. Use `visual` for explanatory lines; never substitute
`action` or `data` merely to get an edge.

`--fresh-context` performs context and build internally and reacquires once on a conclusive pre-apply
stale race. Scope every new request ID to page plus task/run, reuse it only for recovery, and never
share IDs across Boards. Applied or unknown outcomes never get a fresh ID. The handshake reports calls.
With direct semantic tools, use only `board_context -> board_build`: copy `board_build_base`
unchanged, add the stable request, intent, recipe, and only a real selection anchor. Never
reconstruct identity, reuse a pre-mutation revision, or substitute the active tab.

## Stop when the result is authoritative

`board_build` already owns bounded placement, mutation, receipt, saved-object readback, persistence,
and any supported presentation acknowledgement. If `release_summary.status` is `ready`, release
its truthful `message` immediately without another tool or model step. On a completed response:

- Do not call `board_read` to reread the returned owner.
- Do not call `board_verify` unless the response was lost or unknown.
- Do not add `board_present` for one simple artifact.
- Do not reload a non-stateful native object.
- Do not open a browser unless pixels or interaction are an explicit acceptance boundary.

On a conclusive `not_applied` or unsupported-capability response, release the final immediately.
Do not read CLI help, schemas, references, memory, or repository source after the refusal merely to
explain it. Preserve the exact refusal and name the smallest direct product gap; investigate only in
a separate implementation task.

For a timed evaluation, use harness-supplied milestones; do not add timestamp-only tool calls. After
an authoritative result, release immediately. Never inspect task/session history to reconstruct a
missed timestamp; leave it unavailable instead of inflating prompt-to-final latency.

Use only scenario-specific proof:

| Artifact          | Minimum development proof                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Native text/card  | Completed receipt plus built-in readback                                         |
| Mermaid/connector | Receipt/readback; inspect rendered structure only when visibility is required    |
| Code Object       | Receipt/readback plus requested interaction/state; reload only for durable state |
| Batch             | One fixture reset/assert before, raw logs during, one audit/scorecard pass after |

On a `local_workspace_authority` headless target, a Code Object create is staged proof only: accept
durable source/state/geometry readback, report interaction and pixels as unproven, and stop. Do not
open or reload a browser unless the user or frozen scenario explicitly requires live interaction or
pixel proof.

For several artifacts, pipe a strict plan or `{"contract":"board-build-recipe-request/v1","recipe_id":"brief_grid","recipe_version":1,"params":{"heading":"...","columns":2,"cards":[{"title":"...","body":"..."}]}}`
to `board build --fresh-context ... --plan-file - --json`; never chain builds or invent another builder.

A rigid row/grid uses one optional `layout`. Members carry no artifact anchor or recipe placement;
the layout places the measured group relative to an external object or earlier non-member alias.
Mixed-height cards and mixed native/Code Object displays should use this instead of placement chains.
Inline a complete ordinary Code Object create recipe; do not look for a plan-specific source-file
path. Copy this minimum shape and expand each artifact recipe fully—never invent `items` or `nodes`:

```json
{
  "contract": "board-build-plan/v1",
  "artifacts": [{"alias":"title","recipe":{"kind":"native_text","text":"Title","placement":{"target":{"kind":"auto"}}}}, {"alias":"a","recipe":{"kind":"native_card","title":"A","body":"Body"}}, {"alias":"b","recipe":{"kind":"native_card","title":"B","body":"Longer body"}}],
  "connections": [{"kind":"visual","label":"explains","source":{"alias":"a"},"target":{"alias":"b"}}],
  "layout": {"kind":"grid","anchor":{"alias":"title"},"members":["a","b"],"columns":2,"column_gap":48,"row_gap":48,"align":"start","placement":{"clearance":64,"preferred_directions":["below"]}}
}
```

The plan validates fully, mutates once, and returns one multi-owner receipt/readback. Mermaid needs the
live layout engine; absent it, fail closed. See [agent-toolset.md](references/agent-toolset.md) only for tool work.

Clearance is `0..1024`. Relative direction accepts cardinal or diagonal natural terms. Do not open a reference to restate this template.

Add group presentation only when asked to see the composition and acknowledgement does not cover it.

## Code Objects

Routine create is fully specified here; do not open `code-objects.md` unless refining. Trusted TSX
runs in process and is not a security sandbox. One ordinary persisted `FRAME` owns source, state,
geometry, connections, lifecycle, Undo, and reopen. Create with
`kind:code_object`, `operation:create`, `source_format:tsx`, stable `object_key`, `name`, and complete
`source`.

Use `setState(current => ({...current, key: value}))` for durable behavior; local React state is
volatile UI. If the request names an initial/default value that must persist, include it in
`--initial-state` on the first create; a TSX fallback is display logic, not persisted Board state,
and must not trigger a post-create replacement/refine loop. For a trusted file use `--source-file`,
`--object-key`, `--object-name`, dimensions (width 240–1600, height 160–1200), and exactly one of
`--auto-place`, `--placement`, or `--relative-to-name`. Refinement is the exception: read the exact
owner/source/hash first, then use [code-objects.md](references/code-objects.md).
For create, directly export the component as `export default function Name({ state, setState }) { ... }`,
write TSX once, then call `board build --fresh-context --source-file FILE --object-key KEY --object-name
NAME --relative-to-name 'Exact anchor'`; do not inline or JSON-escape the source.

## Targeting and recovery

- Pin runtime instance, workspace, runtime document, stable content document, and page. Runtime
  `document_id` is a tab binding; `content_document_id` is durable identity.
- Use `board list --json` only when exact discovery is genuinely missing or ambiguous.
- Trace is bounded read-only evidence, never mutation authority or persistence proof. Query it only
  for unresolved recent pointing, narration, focus, or sequence references.
- On an unknown mutation outcome, recover the original request ID. Never invent a new request ID or
  blind retry.
- Preserve dirty work. Raw eval never mutates a real user Board.
- Applied, read back, visible, interactive, Undo-safe, durable, integrated, and shipped are separate
  claims. State only what the task actually proved.

## Load deeper guidance only when needed

Use [agent-toolset.md](references/agent-toolset.md) for tool/recovery audits,
[code-objects.md](references/code-objects.md) for refinement, [trace.md](references/trace.md) for
Trace, [modalities.md](references/modalities.md) for routing,
[execution-surfaces.md](references/execution-surfaces.md) for product/runtime diagnosis,
[workspace-and-flows.md](references/workspace-and-flows.md) for composition,
[visual-direction.md](references/visual-direction.md) for pixels,
[proof-and-diagnosis.md](references/proof-and-diagnosis.md) for proof, and
[evals.md](references/evals.md) for evaluation.

## Completion

Report the exact target, chosen medium, useful outcome, checks actually run, and one honest remaining
limitation. Keep implementation noise out unless requested.

When revising this skill, read [evals.md](references/evals.md), run `scripts/validate_skill.py`, and
run the system skill validator.

# i-have-adhd

The reader has ADHD. Output is not just brief. It is shaped so an ADHD brain can act on it.

## What ADHD changes about reading

Five facts drive every rule below:

1. Working memory is small. Anything not on screen is forgotten. Do not ask the reader to "keep in mind X."
2. Knowing the answer is not doing the answer. The friction between "got it" and "done it" is where work dies.
3. Starting is the hardest step. The first action must be obvious, small, and doable now.
4. Time estimates feel uniform. "A bit of work" and "a few hours" register the same. Vague estimates fail.
5. Dopamine is scarce. Visible progress matters. Buried wins do not register.

## Rules

### 1. Lead with the next action

The first line is something the reader can do. Not context. Not a plan. The action.

Bad: "Let's think about this. Your auth flow has a few moving pieces..."
Good: "Run `npm install jsonwebtoken`, then edit `src/auth.ts:42`."

If the answer is a command, path, or snippet, it goes first. Prose comes after, if at all.

### 2. Number multi-step tasks

If the work takes more than one step, write a numbered list. Each step is one bounded action. No step contains "and then" twice.

Bad: "First open the file, find the function, swap it out, then run the tests."

Good:
```
1. Open `src/auth.ts`
2. Replace `verifyToken` (lines 42 to 58) with the snippet below
3. Run `npm test -- auth.spec.ts`
```

### 3. End with one concrete next action

If anything is left open, name ONE thing the reader can do in under two minutes. Even "open the file" counts.

Bad: "Hope that helps. Let me know if you want to dig deeper."
Good: "Next: run `npm test` and paste the first failing line."

### 4. Suppress tangents

If a second issue exists, finish the first, then offer the second as a separate question.

Bad: "Here's the fix. By the way, your dependency is also stale, and your README is out of date, and..."
Good: "Here's the fix. Separately: there is also a stale dependency. Want me to handle that next?"

### 5. Restate state every turn

The reader cannot hold "we are on step 3 of 5" between messages. Restate it.

Bad: "Done. Ready for the next part?"
Good: "Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated. Next: backfill the new column. Run the script?"

### 6. Give specific time estimates

Vague estimates fail. Ballpark in concrete units.

Bad: "This will take some work."
Good: "About 15 minutes if tests already cover this. An afternoon if not."

### 7. Make completed work visible

Show what now works, in concrete terms. Do not bury wins in a recap.

Bad: "I've made some changes to the auth flow. Among other things..."
Good: "Login now works with magic links. Try: `npm run dev`, open `/login`."

### 8. Matter-of-fact tone for errors

Never use "Uh oh," "Oh no," or "There seems to be a problem." State cause and fix.

Bad: "Uh oh, the test is failing. There seems to be an issue..."
Good: "Test fails at `auth.spec.ts:42`: expected 200, got 401. Cause: missing auth header. Fix: add `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` to the request."

### 9. Cap lists at 5 items

If a list grows past five, split into "do now" vs "later," or "must" vs "nice to have." Five items ranked beats ten unranked.

### 10. No preamble, no recap, no closing pleasantries

Forbidden openers: "Great question," "Let me...", "I'll...", "Sure!", "Looking at your...", "To answer your question..."

Forbidden recaps after a completed task: "I've now done X, Y, and Z, which means..."

Forbidden closers: "Let me know if you need anything else," "Hope this helps," "Happy to clarify," "Feel free to ask."

Start with the answer. End when the answer is done.

## When to break the rules

Override the defaults when:

1. User asks to "explain" or "walk me through." Explain fully. Still no preamble, still no closer, but the body runs as long as the topic needs. Add headers so the reader can skim back.
2. Destructive action ahead (`rm -rf`, force push, schema migration, dropping a table). Confirm before acting. Safety wins over brevity.
3. Debug spiral. If the last three turns have been "still broken," stop iterating on code. Name the assumption that might be wrong. Ask one diagnostic question.
4. Real ambiguity in the request. One short clarifying question beats guessing and rewriting.

## Pre-send check

Before sending, delete:

1. The first sentence if it announces what you are about to do.
2. The last sentence if it asks "anything else?" or recaps what just happened.
3. Any "by the way" sidebar.
4. Any hedging adverb adding no information ("perhaps," "might," "could possibly").

Then verify: if the reader reads only the first line and the last line, do they know (a) what to do next, and (b) what just happened?

If yes, send.

- Symptom: remote control setup repeatedly fails. Cause: account MFA was required, not a generic network failure. Fix: inspect the exact rejection, enable MFA with user authorization, then complete the desktop-app pairing flow; do not claim phone approval occurred until it is visible. [Task 8] [chronicle memory]
- Symptom: an empty Trace-space build uses a slow manual path or a good write is reported as fast. Cause: the builder needs an anchor or stale runtime/context triggered recovery. Fix: resolve Trace and Board context in parallel, permit a guarded placement packet at the empty region, and report total journey time separately from raw mutation time. [Task 9] [chronicle memory]
- Symptom: Trace status is reported as live-proven. Cause: the implementation thread drifted into unrelated Board-builder work and canonical live interaction proof was not clearly completed. Fix: say “implemented in source; canonical live acceptance pending/unconfirmed”; do not claim unavailable screen capture or recap-panel updates succeeded. [Task 10]
- Symptom: Board tools return `no_app` when no editor tab is open. Cause: server/CLI hard-coded live-editor registration despite persisted workspace/page authority. Fix: route exact saved-graph operations through `local_workspace_authority`; keep live-only operations explicitly refused rather than blocking durable read/write. [Task 10] [chronicle memory]
- Symptom: a current-source Board-builder run is described as visually/live accepted. Cause: earlier accepted evidence was conflated with the current dirty-checkout rerun, whose exact `http://127.0.0.1:1420/` tab showed `This page crashed`. Fix: require a manual Reload in that exact tab and rerun the acceptance harness; do not substitute another Board, port, or browser. [Task 11]
- Symptom: uncertain mutation is retried with a new request ID, or delete loses its receipt. Cause: replay identity was discarded, or persistence started before receipt storage. Fix: recover with the same request ID or `board_verify`, and store the receipt before the first post-effect `await`. [Task 11]
- Symptom: a browser-created “new Board” pollutes the canonical workspace, or fast Board CLI timing is treated as the agent journey. Fix: use an isolated/named evaluation Board, avoid UI creation for mass tests, and record prompt-to-final timing plus failures separately from mutation latency. [Task 12] [chronicle memory]
- Symptom: an evaluator treats `board build --help` as a mutation, or executor crashes silently remove an attempt. Cause: command classification/ledger handling is wrong. Fix: classify help as non-mutating and retain an append-only `run_error` record. [Task 13] [chronicle memory]
- Symptom: `board edit --operation delete` is advertised but refuses or a call times out after reload/HMR. Cause: the running editor lacks `board.change.object.delete`, or the runtime ID/context became stale. Fix: wire the real capability, reacquire the exact visible writer, and recover the original request ID before any duplicate proof call. [Task 13] [chronicle memory]

Fix: route normal saved-graph mutations through central persisted authority; connected windows synchronize, while same-object/property conflicts and stale saves still refuse safely.
